useCase.name: Import many students at once from a spreadsheet

intent.name: student.import.run
intent.summary: Create the students from the valid rows of a validated import batch, leaving the rejected rows reported and uncreated. One step, and each row stands or falls on its own.
routesHere: import the valid rows from this batch

routesHere.text: file check ho gayi hai, import chala do
routesHere.gloss: the file has been checked, run the import

routesHere.text: jo rows sahi hain wo import kar do
routesHere.gloss: import the rows that are correct

routesHere: go ahead and create the 398 valid students

routesElsewhere.note: Uploading needs the file itself and the request channel carries no file. The upload and the validation happen on the screen; what a plan can do is run, authorise or cancel a batch that is already there.
A batch above the row threshold creates nothing until a School Admin authorises it (BR-12, A1).

request.gloss: I need to add one student

routesElsewhere.note: A student record is never created by typing (UC-03-01 BR-1). One student arrives through admission; an import is a migration path for a whole cohort (BR-1).

request.text: import ke baad ek record theek karna hai
request.gloss: I need to correct a record after the import

routesElsewhere.note: Correcting an imported record is the ordinary maintenance path, not part of the import.

steps.note: One step. Every row was validated before this was reachable (BR-3), so nothing here discovers on row 300 that the file was wrong. The rejected rows are already known and are not attempted.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The authorisation threshold, the batch's status and whether existing roll numbers were supplied are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors. A batch above the threshold is not refused — it is sent for School Admin authorisation (E9), which is an outcome to report rather than a failure.
plan.atomicity: Two different guarantees, and they matter separately. Each row is atomic: it produces a complete student, guardian, family and enrolment, or it produces nothing at all, so a row that fails while its guardian is being created leaves no fragment behind (BR-11, E8, AC-8). The batch is not atomic: valid rows are created and rejected rows are reported with their row number and reason, and one bad row never stops the rest (BR-4). So a partial result is the normal shape here. Rows already created by an earlier run of the same file are recognised and skipped rather than duplicated (BR-13, A6).

errors.meaning: The row count is above the threshold a Staff user may import unaided.
errors.written: Nothing. The validated file is frozen so it cannot change while it waits (A1).
errors.note: Not a failure. Report that it has gone to School Admin for authorisation and that nothing has been created (AC-10). Never split the file to get under the threshold.

errors.meaning: A Staff user ran a file supplying existing roll numbers.
errors.note: Only a School Admin may import with existing roll numbers (BR-10, A4).

errors.meaning: No row in the file could be imported.
errors.written: Nothing. The batch completes with a report.
errors.note: Message points at the report. This is an answer about the file, not a failure of the run.

errors.meaning: A row failed part way through creation.
errors.written: Nothing for that row — no student, no guardian, no enrolment (BR-11, AC-8). Every other row is unaffected.
errors.note: Reported in rejected with its row number. The row is atomic, so there is no fragment to clean up.

errors.meaning: The batch has not finished validating, or has already run.
errors.note: UC-03-03 defines no exception for it because the run control is only offered on a validated batch. See OPEN-QUESTIONS.

planningRules.rule: Report the counts before the plan is emitted, and never run a batch the actor has not seen the size of. This creates student records, guardian portal accounts and fee liability for a whole cohort at once, and none of it can be uncreated.

Never split a file to get under the authorisation threshold. The threshold exists so a School Admin sees a large import before it runs (BR-12); two batches under it create the same students with nobody having looked.

Report the three counts separately — created, rejected, skipped — and name the rejected rows. A batch reported as a success hides the rows BR-4 insists on listing, and the actor has a corrected file to prepare.

Never treat a rejected row as something to fix in the plan. An ambiguous date is rejected rather than guessed (BR-5), a duplicate identity number names the existing record (BR-6), a full section is not over-filled (BR-9). Each is the file being wrong, and the fix is a corrected file.

Never re-run a batch to retry the rejected rows. Re-running recognises what already succeeded and skips it (BR-13), but the rejected rows are still rejected — they need correcting in the file and re-uploading, which is a screen act.

Never plan an import to add one student, or a handful. This path exists deliberately outside the inquiry, approval and test (BR-1); using it for a child who should go through admission bypasses every check that pipeline exists to make.
branch_id and session_id come from $session. A file is imported into the branch and academic session the controller holds, never one named in the request.

reversal.statement: There is none. An import creates students with generated IDs and roll numbers that are never reused, guardian accounts, family codes, enrolments and fee liability. Undoing it means deactivating each record, which is UC-03-01's business, refused outright where a fee transaction already references one (UC-03-01 BR-11). The controller must not attempt a compensating call, and must not re-run the batch in the hope of correcting it — a re-run skips what exists rather than replacing it.

resolvedPlans.outcome: 398 students exist, each with a generated student ID and roll number. The 14 rejected rows come back with their row numbers and reasons for a corrected file (AC-1). Report all three numbers; a bare "import complete" hides the 14.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is created. The validated file is frozen so it cannot change while it waits, and School Admin has the authorisation request (AC-10). Report that plainly — the actor will otherwise assume 900 students now exist.

intent.name: student.import.authorise

jo import approval ka intezaar kar raha hai, wo chala do
routesHere.gloss: run the import that is waiting for approval

routesHere: yes, go ahead with the 900-row import

routesElsewhere.note: A batch below the threshold runs without authorisation.
Declining an authorisation is a cancellation, and the batch is not run.

Uploading needs the file itself and the request channel carries no file. The upload and the validation happen on the screen; what a plan can do is run, authorise or cancel a batch that is already there.

steps.note: One step, and it runs the import. Authorising is not an approval that sits waiting — it is the act that creates the students, so everything the run contract says about counts and per-row atomicity applies here too.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The acting role and the batch's status are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: The same two guarantees as the run: each row atomic, the batch not (BR-4, BR-11). Authorising creates the students immediately, so a partial result is the normal shape and the rejected rows are reported with their reasons. The file was frozen at validation and could not change while it waited (A1), so what is created is what the School Admin was shown.

errors.meaning: The batch is not waiting for authorisation.
errors.note: It has already run, been cancelled, or was never above the threshold. UC-03-03 defines no exception for it — see OPEN-QUESTIONS.

planningRules.rule: Report what is being authorised before the plan is emitted — the row count, who uploaded it and how many rows were rejected at validation. Authorising is not a formality: it creates the students immediately.

Never authorise a batch the acting user uploaded themselves without saying so. The threshold exists so a second person looks at a large import (BR-12), and a School Admin authorising their own file is within their rights but worth stating.

Never chain an authorisation onto a run that was refused for the threshold. E9 sends the batch to a School Admin, and authorising it in the same breath — in a session that happens to hold both capabilities — removes the second pair of eyes the threshold exists to insert.
Report the rejected rows exactly as the run contract does. Authorising a 900-row file and reporting a success hides the rows BR-4 insists on listing.

intent.name: student.import.cancel
intent.summary: Cancel a validated import batch before it runs, so nothing is created. One step.
routesHere: cancel that import, the file was wrong

routesHere.text: import cancel kar do, file galat thi
routesHere.gloss: cancel the import, the file was wrong

routesHere.text: ye batch chhod do, nayi file bhejunga
routesHere.gloss: drop this batch, I will send a new file

request.text: jo import ho chuki hai use undo kar do
request.gloss: undo the import that already ran

routesElsewhere.note: Cancelling is only possible before the rows are created. Once students exist, undoing means deactivating each record, which is UC-03-01's business and refused where a fee transaction references one.

Uploading needs the file itself and the request channel carries no file. The upload and the validation happen on the screen; what a plan can do is run, authorise or cancel a batch that is already there.

steps.note: One step, and it is only reachable before the rows are created. A batch that has run cannot be cancelled — there is nothing left to stop.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the batch has already run is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write: the batch moves to Cancelled and the audit entry is written, together or not at all. No student, guardian, family or enrolment is created or removed — the batch never created any. The uploaded file and its validation report stay readable, so the rejected rows can still be corrected for a fresh upload.

operations.name: student.import.cancel
operations.idempotencyKey: batch_id, since a batch has one cancellation and a repeat returns ALREADY_CANCELLED
operations.purpose: Cancel a validated or pending batch so its rows are never created, keeping the file and its validation report.

parameters.name: batch_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No import batch matches in this branch at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with file name, upload time, row count and status. Two files uploaded the same morning is the ordinary case.

parameters.notes: The import batch, resolved from how the actor named it — the file name, the upload time, or simply the most recent one. It exists because someone uploaded a file on the screen; a plan cannot create one.

parameters.name: cancel_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 250 characters. Only where the request gives one. Not required by the use case, but it is what someone reads when they find a cancelled batch later.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: batch_id
fields.description: The batch cancelled.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Cancelled. Terminal.

fields.name: rows_read
fields.description: What the file held, kept for reference.

fields.name: cancelled_by
fields.description: The acting user.

fields.name: validation_report_available
fields.description: The rejected rows and their reasons stay readable for a corrected file.

errors.meaning: The batch has already been imported.
errors.note: Students exist and cancelling does not remove them. UC-03-03 defines no exception for it because the cancel control is only offered before the run — see OPEN-QUESTIONS.
Cancelled is terminal. Not a failure to retry.

planningRules.rule: Never cancel a batch to deal with rejected rows. Rejected rows create nothing anyway (BR-4), and the valid ones are worth importing — cancelling throws away the good rows to avoid the bad ones.

Never treat ALREADY_RUN as an undo. Cancelling stops a batch from running; it does not remove students that exist. Where the wrong cohort was imported, that is a deactivation problem on each record, not a cancellation.
Never chain a cancellation onto a failed run. A run that reported rejected rows still created the valid ones, and cancelling afterwards changes nothing while suggesting it did.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Cancelled is terminal. A cancelled batch is not re-run — the file is corrected and uploaded afresh, which is a screen act. Nothing was created, so there is nothing to undo either way.

steps.note: The plan is emitted unchanged; it does not check the status beforehand. The API returns ALREADY_RUN.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing changes. Report that the batch has already run and 398 students exist — cancelling does not remove them, and removing them is a different and much harder act (PR-2).

inputs.cancel_reason: Deferred until the new session opens.

resolvedPlans.outcome: The batch is cancelled and the authorisation request is withdrawn with it. The file will need uploading again afterwards, because Cancelled is terminal.

routesHere: what's the status of the pending import batch

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Row scope is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: A read. Nothing is created, changed or cancelled, and nothing is written.

planningRules.rule: Say which batch was read whenever the request named none. "How did the import go" resolves to the most recent, and a school running two files in a morning gets the wrong answer silently otherwise.
Report created, rejected and skipped as three numbers, never as one. A batch of 412 that created 398 is not a success or a failure; it is both, and the 14 need a corrected file (BR-4, AC-1).
